content.title: Tax Day 2026: When are taxes due? How to file, get extension
content.text: More than 90% of taxpayers are expected to file electronically, according to the Tax Policy Center, while the Internal Revenue Service processes more than 150 million individual returns each year.Gabe Ginsberg/Getty ImagesTaxes are due Wednesday and millions of Americans are racing to file before the deadline.More than 90% of taxpayers are expected to file electronically, according to the Tax Policy Center, while the Internal Revenue Service processes more than 150 million individual returns each year.Article continues below this adGet Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.Get Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.ONLY 25¢The IRS began accepting returns Jan. 26. Taxpayers who file on time can typically receive refunds within weeks — but only if they submit their returns correctly and on time.Here’s what to know about the 2026 tax deadline, how long refunds take and how to track your money.When is the tax filing deadline in 2026?The federal tax deadline is April 15, 2026.Article continues below this adTaxpayers living outside the U.S. and Puerto Rico on April 15 receive an automatic two-month extension to file their 2025 returns, moving the deadline to June 15.Electronic returns must be submitted by 11:59 p.m. local time on the deadline. Paper returns must be properly addressed, postmarked and include sufficient postage.How long does it take to get a tax refund in 2026?Most refunds are issued in fewer than three weeks, according to the IRS.Article continues below this adFiling electronically and choosing direct deposit is the fastest way to get a refund. Paper returns and mailed checks can take significantly longer.The IRS advises taxpayers not to rely on receiving a refund by a specific date, especially for major purchases or bill payments, because some returns require additional review.Need more time? According to the IRS, there are three ways to get an extension to file your tax return.Article continues below this ad Use Free File (no income limit for extensions): Use IRS Free File to electronically request an automatic tax-filing extension. Request an extension by mail: File Form 4868, Application for Automatic Extension of Time To File U.S. Individual Income Tax Return. You can file by mail, online with an IRS e-filing partner or through a tax professional. Estimate how much tax you owe for the year on the extension form: Subtract the taxes you already paid for the filing year. Pay online and check the box: Pay what you owe using an online payment option and check the box that you are paying as part of filing for an extension. You don’t have to file a separate extension form and you’ll receive a confirmation number of your extension for your records. I'm out of the country? Can I still get an extension?You may get an automatic two-month extension if you’re a U.S. citizen or resident alien on the regular due date of your tax return and living out of the country.Where's my refund? How to check your tax return statusTaxpayers can track their refund using the IRS “Where’s My Refund?” tool at IRS.gov.Article continues below this adTo see the status, taxpayers must enter the following information: Your Social Security or individual taxpayer ID number (ITIN) Your filing status The exact refund amount on your return Once the information is entered, the tool will display one of three statuses: Return Received — The IRS has your return and is processing it. Refund Approved — Your refund has been approved and is scheduled for payment. Refund Sent — The IRS has issued your refund. Direct deposits may take up to five days to appear; mailed checks can take several weeks. Article continues below this adWhy is my IRS tax refund delayed?There can be many reasons why a tax return is delayed. Here are the most common reasons, according to the IRS: The return has errors, is incomplete, or is affected by identity theft or fraud. The return needs a correction to the child tax credit or recovery rebate credit amount. The return has a claim filed for an earned income tax credit or additional child tax credit or includes a Form 8379, Injured Spouse Allocation. The time it takes a taxpayer's bank or credit union to post the refund to the taxpayer's account. Will 2026 tax refunds be larger?President Donald Trump has said refunds this year could be larger due to his “One Big Beautiful Bill” tax cuts enacted last year.Article continues below this adIn a Feb. 17 post on Truth Social, Trump wrote that refunds are “substantially greater than ever before,” adding that in some cases “over 20% will be returned to the Taxpayer.”The Bipartisan Policy Center has projected that the legislation could generate billions in retroactive tax relief, with a portion distributed through refunds and another portion offsetting tax liabilities.Actual refund amounts vary based on income, tax withholdings and individual tax situations.Article continues below this adStories you won't want to miss, handpicked by Statesman editors.April 14, 2026Marley Malenfant is a 10-year multimedia journalist who’s worked in print, digital, and broadcast. His prior work includes working in West Texas as a TV reporter for KTXS. During his time there, he covered education, sports, features, and breaking News. He’s skilled in front of the camera as well as behind it. He was a freelance writer, published in D Magazine, Dallas Morning News, SB Nation, Dallas Observer, and was a personality for “The Coach Brothers” sports radio show. Outside of journalism, he was an educator in the Dallas area. He was a 2012 Mayborn Literary Nonfiction Conference grant recipient. In 2021, he was part of the NABJ student multimedia project. He graduated with a paralegal degree from El Centro in 2023. Currently, he’s a trending news reporter for the Austin American-Statesman, covering breaking News, sports, music, and legal trends.
